series_key: mql4 language for newbies. custom indicators
mechanism: Signal indicator reads another custom buffer via iCustom; when value>upper level (800) write High+offset into DRAW_ARROW buy buffer else empty; when value<lower level (200) write Low-offset into sell arrow buffer else empty—level-crossing change sensor on chart.
data_needed: Compiled custom indicator EX4 in experts/indicators; iCustom(symbol,tf,name,params,mode,shift); two arrow buffers with SetIndexEmptyValue; fixed levels (article: 800/200).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Active chart Symbol()/period via iCustom(NULL,0,...); RandomIndicator example with barsToProcess; MT4 bars
why_new_for_mis: Shows a clean buffer-level crossing change sensor that turns any custom series into buy/sell arrow events MIS can consume without reinventing signal plumbing.
quote: if a line moves above the upper level (800.0), buy; if a line moves below the lower level (200.0), sell

series_key: mql4 language for newbies. custom indicators
mechanism: On each start(), counted_bars=IndicatorCounted(); if>0 decrement; limit=Bars-counted_bars (capped by barsToProcess); loop only i<limit so only new/changed bars update buffers—incremental sensing refresh.
data_needed: IndicatorCounted(); Bars; optional extern barsToProcess limiter; bound indicator buffers.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any chart Symbol/TF the indicator is attached to; MT4 tick-driven start()
why_new_for_mis: Operationalizes incremental bar-window sensing so MIS sensors recompute only the live edge instead of full-history every tick.
quote: First an indicator is calculated on all available candlesticks, and only then when quotes are received, it will recalculate the value only for the last candlestick.

series_key: mql4 language for newbies. custom indicators
mechanism: 9×3 OBJ_LABEL Wingdings grid in pixel coords (OBJPROP_XDISTANCE/YDISTANCE, OBJPROP_CORNER) stays chart-fixed; columns=period[] {M1..MN1}; rows=MA(13>24), |WPR|<20/>80, SAR vs Close; color squares green/red/gray encode multi-TF regime concurrence.
data_needed: iMA/iWPR/iSAR per Symbol() and period[x]; OBJ_LABEL grid; extern scale/offset/colors/symbol codes.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Chart Symbol(); periods M1,M5,M15,M30,H1,H4,D1,W1,MN1 simultaneously; MA 13/24, WPR 13, SAR 0.02/0.2
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a compact multi-timeframe regime concurrence board (trend/oscillator/stop) that does not drift with price/time scrolling—usable as a live cross-TF sensor panel.
quote: A trader constantly estimates a situation in the market the following way: the market should be entered when signals come from each of the three indicators

mechanism: EX5 library exports ErrorAdvisor retry policy, TradingIsAllowed checks, OpenBuy/SellPosition, SetSlTpByTicket, ClosePositionByTicket—trade execution tooling, not market sensing.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any symbol passed to open/close helpers; no sensing TF
why_new_for_mis: No market sensing after full read—position open/close/SLTP execution library only.
quote: Position management is a fundamental task for every Expert Advisor under development.

mechanism: Dual Variable Index Dynamic Average handles: fast (lower params) vs slow (higher params); buy when fast line above slow, sell when fast below slow; gates OpenBuy/Sell and optional CloseAllProfitable* on crossover—trend-regime sensor driving the toolkit.
data_needed: Two iVIDyA (or VIDYA) indicator handles with distinct cmo/ema periods; buffer[0]/[1] comparison each tick.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EA chart _Symbol and chart TF; DualVidyaTrader demo; magic-filtered positions
why_new_for_mis: Concrete adaptive-MA crossover regime sensor MIS can reuse as a trend gate, demonstrated live against the positions toolkit.
quote: For a buy entry, the "fast VIDyA" line must be above the "slow VIDyA" line, and for a sell entry, the "fast VIDyA" line must be below the "slow VIDyA" line.

mechanism: GetPositionsData() scans PositionsTotal each call and fills globals: buy/sell counts, volumes, and profits sliced by account / magic / symbol—exportable BuyPositionsTotal, SymbolPositionsProfit, AccountPositionsStatus, etc. as live book sensors.
data_needed: Open positions via PositionGetTicket/String/Integer/Double; optional symbol+magic filters; ACCOUNT_CURRENCY for display.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: All account symbols or filtered _Symbol+magic; tick-time (no chart TF)
why_new_for_mis: Turns fragmented position APIs into one-line exposure/PnL sensors MIS can poll as portfolio-state inputs.
quote: having a clear and straightforward overview of all open positions is critical for the success of your trading system. However, there are no straight out-of-the-box standard language functions that provide this information.

mechanism: EX5 library OpenBuy/Sell Limit/Stop, ModifyPendingOrderByTicket, DeletePending* with MAX_ORDER_RETRIES/ORDER_RETRY_DELAYS—pending-order execution tooling only.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Symbol stop levels/spread for entry validation; no sensing TF
why_new_for_mis: No market sensing after full read—pending order place/modify/delete library only.

mechanism: HistorySelect→SaveDealsData/SaveOrdersData; SavePositionsData walks DEAL_ENTRY_OUT deals, matches DEAL_ENTRY_IN by POSITION_ID, enriches from filled orders; computes duration, netProfit=profit+swap−commission, pipProfit/slPips/tpPips, initiatedByPendingOrder flag—reconstructed trade-performance sensor rows.
data_needed: HistorySelect(from,to); HistoryDealGet*/HistoryOrderGet*; SYMBOL_POINT for pip math; PositionData struct array.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any traded symbols in account history; server-time windows; no chart TF required
why_new_for_mis: Fills MQL5’s missing HistoryPosition* gap with POSITION_ID-joined closed-trade metrics MIS can use as post-trade performance sensors.
quote: we need to create a custom function that combines orders and deals data, using the Position ID as the connecting key to link deals with their originating orders.

mechanism: FetchHistoryByCriteria starts last 24h, widens by weeks up to 53 then full account (epoch→now) until target array nonempty; GetLastClosedPositionData exposes type/volume/profit/netProfit/pipProfit/duration/SL-TP pips for the newest closed position as one-call sensors.
data_needed: GetHistoryData + GET_POSITIONS_HISTORY_DATA; positionInfo[0] after reverse-chronology save; referenced out-params.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Account trade history symbols; adaptive lookback from 1D→1Y→all
why_new_for_mis: Adaptive history-window fetch plus last-closed metric getters give MIS cheap, always-available trade-outcome sensors without manual date ranges.
quote: it begins by checking the most recent data, and if no relevant history is found, it progressively scans older data—first by week, up to a year.

mechanism: GetLastFilledPendingOrderData after FetchHistoryByCriteria(GET_PENDING_ORDERS_HISTORY_DATA); expose type/symbol/ticket/priceOpen/sl-tp pips plus timeSetup and timeDone so callers can measure broker fill latency (timeDone−timeSetup) and order-type mix.
data_needed: Pending orders history with ORDER_STATE_FILLED; PendingOrderData fields timeSetup/timeDone/type.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Symbols of filled pendings in account history; event times on trade server clock
why_new_for_mis: Turns last-filled pending timestamps into an execution-quality/latency sensor MIS can track alongside strategy logic.
quote: examining details like slippage, the time elapsed from order placement to execution, and the conditions under which the order was filled, you can identify patterns

mechanism: GetLastCanceledPendingOrderData finds ORDER_STATE_CANCELED; LastCanceledPendingOrderTimeSetup/TimeDone pair yields open-to-cancel duration; also type/reason/filling/typeTime for cancel analytics.
data_needed: Pending orders history with canceled state; timeSetup and timeDone fields.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Symbols of canceled pendings in account history; server timestamps

quote: For tasks requiring the calculation of the total time a pending order was open before being canceled, this function can be used alongside the LastCanceledPendingOrderTimeSetup() function.
